1.w: [“] Man, born of a woman, [is] short of days and full of trouble.

2.w: Like a flower he comes forth and withers, and he flees like a shadow, and does not stand.

3.w: And upon this one do You open Your eyes; and bring me into judgment with You?

4.w: Who will bring clean from unclean? Not one!

5.w: Since his days are determined, the number of his months [is] with You; his limits You have made, and he cannot pass over [them].

6.w: Look away from him that he may rest, until he can enjoy his day like a hireling.

7.w: For there is hope for a tree, if it is cut down, that again it will pass through, and its tender shoots will not cease.

8.w: Though its root may grow old in the earth, and its stump may die in the dirt,

9.w: from the scent of water it will sprout, and will make branch[es] like a [fresh] planting.

10.w: And a man dies and is laid low; and a man expires, and where [is] he?

11.w: As waters disappear from the sea, and a river dries up and withers,

12.w: so a man lies down and does not arise; until the heavens [are] no more, they will not awaken and they will not be roused from their sleep.

13.w: Who will give [that] You would hide me in Sheol, [that] You would hide me until the turning back of Your anger, [that] You would set for me a limit, and then remember me!

14.w: If a man dies, will he live? All the days of my hardship, I will wait, until the coming of my change.

15.w: You will call, and I will answer You; You will desire the work of Your hands.

16.w: For now, You count my steps; You do not watch over my sin.

17.w: My transgression is sealed up in a bundle, and You plaster over my iniquity.

18.w: But [as] a falling mountain wastes away, and [as] a rock moves from its place,

19.w: [as] stones [by] the waters are worn away, [and] her torrents engulf the dust of the earth, so the hope of man You destroy.

20.w: You prevail over him forever, and he goes away; You change his face and send him away.

21.w: His sons gain honor, and he does not know [it]; and they are diminished, and he does not perceive it.

22.w: Indeed his flesh upon him is in pain, and his soul mourns over him.”
